correctness.rationale: The source ensemble is exactly all qk-length k-universal words. Greedy matching yields a necessary-and-sufficient target-by-target absent criterion with weak rank comparisons. Independence gives the mean; the two-orbit exact tensor calculation provides all four rational entries and a strictly positive transfer matrix. The characteristic polynomial supplies the recurrence, and positive Perron root comparison gives the exponential relative-variance rate. Literal direct subsequence enumeration and independent exact rational covariance checks passed from actual standalone verifier.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: An exact SAS formula for two fixed permutations repeated in blocks, or for a fixed binary run word, only evaluates special deterministic inputs and does not determine cross-input correlations. A maximum is weaker than an ensemble second moment. The all-alphabet random-rank calculation gives new data: a two-class tensor transfer, a universal q-dependent second-order recurrence, and exponentially growing relative variance. The known results provide conceptual tools but none of their stated conclusions imply this average-case law.

value.rationale: All (q!)^k minimal-length k-universal words form a natural exact average-case model for absent subsequences. The formulas evaluate a genuine unaddressed distributional invariant for all alphabets and block counts and reveal exponential growth of the coefficient of variation squared, something no worst-case bound or mean alone explains. This is a natural structural random-matrix phenomenon of string universality, not an arbitrarily chosen finite slice.
